title: Oregon's Nasir Wyatt highlighted as major fall camp riser
description: One of Oregon's rising sophomore linebackers has been identified as a riser through one week of fall camp by CBS Sports.
fullText:
It didn't take Nasir Wyatt far into his freshman season with the Oregon Ducks before he began impressing, as he recorded his first career sack in the Ducks' second game against the Montana State Bobcats. He logged only 39 snaps but made the absolute most of them, finishing the year third on the team with three sacks, a forced fumble and 11 total tackles.

Primarily deployed on third-down blitzes and various pressures, Wyatt used his 6-foot-2, 228-pound frame to blast past would-be blocker and get to the quarterback in a flash. But what proved to be his superpower also turned out to be his downfall, as a sub-230-pound edge rusher had to be schemed into action. If he were to be on the field on early downs, teams would likely target his side and run the ball right at him, capitalizing on his lean frame.

No more in 2026. With his newly-chiseled, bulky frame, Wyatt arrived at fall camp already impressing and has continued that sentiment through one week, with CBS Sports' Brad Crawford tabbing him as one of the biggest risers thus far infall camp.

"From failing to bulk up early in his career to now tipping the scales at a muscular 245 pounds, Wyatt finally looks the part as one of the Ducks' outside linebackers," Crawford wrote. "Defensive coordinator Chris Hampton said after Oregon's second day of fall camp that Wyatt has a chance to be an "every-down player" this fall, which speaks to his offseason body makeover and what he's shown on the field early. That level of consistency must continue, Hampton says, to warrant extended reps at an uber-talented position group for one of the Big Ten's frontrunners."

Reps won't come easy for Wyatt, who, as a hybrid linebacker/edge rusher, is behind starters Matayo Uiagalelei and Teitum Tuioti, two players garnering early-round buzz in the 2027 NFL Draft class.

But during head coach Dan Lanning's tenure, the best players are put on the field regardless of fanfare or draft hype. Whoever will help the Ducks win the most games will be placed on the field.

And in 2026, you bet Wyatt will be on the field plenty more than 39 snaps, making even more of an impact during a potential sophomore breakout.

title: Inside the transgender controversy taking over the WNBA, from Sophie Cunningham’s comments to now
description: WNBA discourse has been recently dominated by the ongoing debate about whether transgender athletes should be allowed in women’s sports, and it’s interesting to see how it got to this point. The WNBA has gotten caught up in a larger cultural issue over the past couple of weeks.
fullText:
WNBA discourse has been recently dominated by the ongoing debate about whether transgender athletes should be allowed in women's sports, and it's interesting to see how it got to this point.

The WNBA has gotten caught up in a larger cultural issue over the past couple of weeks. The topic in question? Whether transgender athletes should be allowed to compete in women's sports.

This culture war controversy has been going on for a long time within the world of sports. But considering that the W has been known for its inclusivity, it hadn't come up in the league's context yet.

However, all that changed with Sophie Cunningham's July comments, which opened up a Pandora's box and led to a chain reaction. Here's a look at the timeline of the entire debate.

Cunningham's rise to WNBA stardom came suddenly after her hard foul while defending superstar Caitlin Clark, and she has only grown more popular since.

In 2022, Cunningham had reposted a comment protesting transgender swimmer Lia Thomas. The backlash on social media was swift, and she released a statement expressing support for all athletes.

Her comments which sparked this recent argument came in an ESPN interview published on July 21.

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans," Cunningham said. "And I'm like, 'I never once said that,'" she says. "I think that I am here to extend love.

"But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

This led to many fans praising for speaking 'the truth' despite it being controversial. Others felt the comments were a bit intolerant and against exclusivity, which led to others in the league speaking out.

The league has long been known as a queer-friendly, inclusive space in the world of sports. It was natural that the Fever player's comments would lead to a response.

Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve wore a t-shirt in support of transgender people, it read, 'Trans kids belong'. And speaking ahead of the Lynx-Fever clash earlier in August, she explained her point.

"I come from a space of inclusion," Reeve told reporters, as per an ESPN report. "The narrative that I think is problematic is to suggest that transgender athletes are the biggest problem in women's sports.

"This is what's bothersome. There is a faction of people in our country that are making this a massive issue."

Golden State Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase added her voice to this view as well.

"For me sports is about belonging," Nakase said. "It's about inclusivity. It's about allowing everyone to be their authentic self. I'm all about women, little girls deserving to play, and that includes trans women."

The two coaches' comments also received pushback, Stephen A. Smith was among those to call out Reeve. While the controversy was only raging within the league at this point, it was about to get some new entrants.

This issue has caused ripples all over the sports world, and some former NBA stars saw the opportunity to involve themselves. Enes Kanter Freedom was the first to do so, wildly declaring for the 2027 WNBA Draft.

"After careful consideration and reviewing the current eligibility guidelines, I'm officially declaring myself a WNBA prospect," Freedom wrote in a post on X.

If simply declaring who you are is all that's required, then I meet every single requirement necessary to compete in the WNBA… Based on the current guidelines, I can and am officially declaring my eligibility for the upcoming WNBA draft."

He wasn't the only person with this idea either, Royce White followed suit just hours later, claiming the same thing.

"I'm transgender. I'm a woman. I identify as sometimes identifying as a woman for purpose of basketball, professional basketball, so I'll be declaring for the WNBA draft in 2027 as well," White said.

The involvement of Freedom and White took the issue to a whole new level. Both have since only doubled down on their messaging, fanning the flames of an already heated social media debate.

The million-dollar question for the WNBA is where things go from here. The WNBPA has already released a statement announcing their stance against discrimination and athletes being excluded.

"Hate, abuse, and demonization of any person or group of people, including transgender people, only fuel fear, division, and harm," the statement reads.

"We will continue to have hard conversations. But we will not be used as political pawns."

The players seem committed to keeping the WNBA inclusive, but the situation might force the league to define their policies in one way or another.

It's a shame that a political issue seems to be overshadowing the game on the court at the moment. Hopefully, the situation will be dealt with soon and fans can get excited for some playoff hoops instead.

His profile is particularly interesting because he is a left-footed centre-back, a characteristic that the La Liga champions value when assessing options for the heart of the defence.

He also brings European experience and could provide Hansi Flick with another reliable option as the coach prepares his squad for the new season.

The departure of Araujo has created an opening in Barcelona's defensive planning.

title: ‘The single worst call in basketball history’: Barstool does not hold back on WNBA refs after Caitlin Clark call
description: Dave Portnoy is on a roll calling out the WNBA. After blasting ESPN and Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White for not defending Sophie Cunningham when she was fouled intentionally by Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington, the Barstool Sports founder was back at it Monday alongside colleague Brandon Walker. Walker and Portnoy took aim at…
fullText:
Dave Portnoy is on a roll calling out the WNBA. After blasting ESPN and Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White for not defending Sophie Cunningham when she was fouled intentionally by Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington, the Barstool Sports founder was back at it Monday alongside colleague Brandon Walker.

Walker and Portnoy took aim at the controversial technical foul against Fever star Caitlin Clark during Saturday's 90-86 win over Chicago. Clark received the tech for making contact with an official, though she had been bumped by the Sky's Natasha Cloud, which caused her to lose her balance. Following the game, crew chief Maj Forsberg said the official "deemed that Clark intentionally made contact; therefore, a technical foul was assessed."

The technical was Clark's eighth of the season, resulting in a suspension for Indiana's next game. However, it was later rescinded by the league.

"Dave, I think what I see right there on the screen is the single worst call in the history of basketball," Walker said Monday morning. "I have never seen anything like it."

Portnoy, who sported an Indiana Fever hat during the segment and is a longtime Caitlin Clark supporter, agreed.

"Yeah, it's brutal," Portnoy said. "And you know what's funny? They have now–and again people are digging up old clips–of that ref actually getting pushed and bodied and not calling it. And then you got Monica McNutt on that other network (ESPN) being like 'I don't know, maybe it was the right call because I saw someone bump into a coach one time.' It's crazy. That call was insane."

Portnoy went on to call it "actually shocking" that the league rescinded the technical, which means Clark won't have to miss any time.

"There was another Caitlin technical where she was mad at herself for missing a shot and she, like, hit the stanchion, and she got a T for that as well," he added. "So listen, the league is out of control, it's off the rails and I can't stop watching.

"I've been preaching now for years that this league is the most passionate. They hate each other, the infighting, the dating, the cultural, the politics…This league, they don't like each other, and it's pretty exciting."

Because the league rescinded the technical foul, Clark is able to play in tomorrow night's showdown against the New York Liberty. Both teams come in having won seven of their last 10 games

title: The transgender row surrounding the WNBA
description: After the Indiana Fever's Sophie Cunningham said it was "common sense" to ban transgender women from women's sports, a row has emerged in the WNBA - with former NBA players saying eligibility rules mean they can enter the 2027 Draft.
fullText:
The WNBA is still in the midst of its 2026 season and yet it is next year's Draft for North America's top women's basketball league that is dominating the headlines.

Why? Because some former men's NBA players have declared they will enter for selection - citing the current eligibility guidelines, or lack of, for transgender women players.

"I'm officially declaring myself a WNBA prospect," said Enes Kanter Freedom, who played 11 seasons in the NBA.

It is the latest development in a story ignited by a comment made by Indiana Fever player Sophie Cunningham, who said she wanted to protect young girls "who shouldn't have to go against biological men" in sport.

Her words have instigated protests - albeit not grand in scale - on both sides of the argument, and once again catapulted the debate around transgender women in sport into the spotlight.

Last month, Cunningham, one of the league's most high-profile players, gave an interview to ESPN, external in which the conversation turned to the topic of "protecting" women's sports.

The Indiana Fever guard said she had received criticism from people who believed she "hated" transgender people, something she denied.

She said she wanted to "extend love" to everyone, but added: "I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

She later doubled down on her comments, saying it was "common sense", external to bar transgender athletes from competing in women's sports.

Her words quickly moved beyond basketball and into a wider political debate in the United States.

President Donald Trump expressed his support for Cunningham, while vice-president JD Vance said she was "inspiring".

Though the 29-year-old later said she is "not a very political person", her remarks have followed her around the country. Competing rallies from critics and supporters were organised at Indiana's games, along with small-scale protests.

The scale of the debate in the media, online and in politics was striking given no openly transgender woman is due to play, or has ever played, in the WNBA.

The WNBA operates under a collective bargaining agreement (CBA), a deal negotiated between the league and its players association (WNBPA), setting rules on matters including player salary caps, revenue sharing, benefits and overall league operations.

On player eligibility, the CBA states: "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA."

The WNBA has yet to comment publicly on the row since Cunningham's comments but league commissioner Cathy Engelbert reportedly sent a memo to teams last week in which she said the matter would be discussed at an upcoming pre-arranged meeting with team presidents.

In the memo, seen by the Associated Press, external, Engelbert said the league would "always approach this topic thoughtfully, respectfully, and in alignment with the longstanding values of our league".

She added: "Our player eligibility rules, unlike the eligibility rules of some other leagues and governing bodies, are collectively bargained. Preserving the integrity of our game and ensuring fair competition will always remain among the league's highest priorities."

However, the lack of detail in the league's eligibility criteria has been brought to light by Kanter Freedom, who finished his playing career with the Boston Celtics in 2022.

"If simply declaring who you are is all that's required, then I meet every single requirement necessary to compete in the WNBA," he wrote on Instagram, external.

Kanter Freedom, who has previously spoken out about human rights violations in China and Turkey, among other issues, added: "I know my presence on the court will stir up strong opinions. I am definitely not here to mock, make fun of, or disrespect any community or personal choices.

"I'm simply asking that the current rules be applied equally to everyone - the rules that represent the very values many WNBA players and coaches have publicly advocated for."

A day after Kanter Freedom's 'announcement', Royce White - who made three appearances in the NBA as a player and is now a Republican Senate candidate - said he would also declare for the Draft, adding: "I identify as sometimes identifying as a woman for purpose of basketball."

Whether the vagueness of the rules are by design to leave it open to transgender women or a sign of an oversight that genuinely needs tightening up is not clear.

BBC Sport has contacted Cunningham's representatives, the WNBA and WNBPA for comment.

Cunningham's comments have become a flashpoint inside a league which has a long history of player activism on issues including race, gender equality and LGBTQ+ rights.

The players' association did not mention Cunningham by name when it eventually addressed the debate.

In a statement the WNBPA denounced "hate abuse and demonisation of the transgender community" and reaffirmed its commitment to "justice, equity, diversity and inclusion".

It called on fans to report abusive behaviour at games and added that it would continue to have "hard" conversations but it "will not be used as political pawns".

There is strong feeling on both sides of the argument. Minnesota Lynx head coach and president Cheryl Reeve, who said: "I come from a space of inclusion.

"The narrative that I think is problematic is to suggest that transgender athletes are the biggest problem in women's sports."

Reeve wore a "Trans Kids Belong" T-shirt before Minnesota played Indiana earlier this month and was seen speaking to Cunningham on court before the game.

Cunningham later said the pair had exchanged their perspectives and that the conversation ended with "love and respect".

Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams said she would welcome a transgender athlete "on my team or against my team, any time".

Last month, the WNBA suspended Seattle Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton from attending the team's next five home games after an exchange with two fans, who were sat courtside displaying signs thanking Cunningham for "speaking up for girls".

Keaton reportedly confronted the teenage fans and admonished them during the game. The Storm have since apologised.

As for Cunningham, the attention has increasingly become an unwelcome distraction.

Having defended her original comments, she said recently that she now wanted the conversation to return to what was happening on court.

"I want to get back to basketball, it's always been about basketball" she said, arguing that the standard of play in the WNBA was being overshadowed by issues away from the game.

But that may prove difficult, as pressure grows on the league to clarify exactly who is eligible to play.

In recent years, many governing bodies in sport have amended their rules about the inclusion of transgender athletes at the elite level, moving more towards restrictions.

Athletics, cycling and aquatics, for example, have implemented outright bans on transgender women taking part in women's events.

In March, it was announced that the women's category of Olympic sports will be limited to biological females from the LA Olympic Games in 2028.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) says eligibility will be determined by a "once-in-a-lifetime" sex test, which would prevent transgender women and those with differences in sexual development (DSD) who have gone through male puberty from competing.

In the United States, transgender women and girls are banned from competing in women's sports categories in schools, universities and the grassroots level.

That was part of an executive order - titled "Keeping Men Out of Women's Sports" - signed by President Trump last year.

It does not cover professional sport.

title: Dana White shares bizarre reason behind ring card girl exclusion
description: The inclusion of ring card girls at big combat sports events has been a custom for decades, but that could now be another change fans will have to get used to following Zuffa Boxing 10. Zuffa Boxing is Dana White's new passion, seemingly pouring his all into the resurection of a once beautiful ...
fullText:
The inclusion of ring card girls at big combat sports events has been a custom for decades, but that could now be another change fans will have to get used to following Zuffa Boxing 10.

Zuffa Boxing is Dana White's new passion, seemingly pouring his all into the resurection of a once beautiful sport. White and his partners have an idea on how to make their promotion click; signing big names and putting on even bigger fights is one way to grab fans' attention and steal viewers from the competition. However, for what seems like the first time in modern history, a global boxing event didn't feature ring girls, but the reason why is highly unusual.

Callum Walsh remained undefeated, strolling his way to a unanimous decision, while fellow countryman Aaron McKenna handed prospect Etinosa Oliha his first professional loss on his way to capturing the vacant IBF world middleweight title. It's safe to say Zuffa Boxing 10 didn't disappoint, delivering a massive night of fights at the 3Arena on Saturday. However, boxing tradition was missing one key component.

The ring aprons were bare after the exclusion of ring card girls. Appearing ringside on a live broadcast with the popular Nina Drama, White was questioned about why the event lacked its usual ring card girls. As he has come accustomed to, White did not hold back his frustrations, saying:

"Don't even get me started," White said in response to the lack of ring card girls at Zuffa Boxing 10. "The UK won't use ring card girls unless you have ring card boys."

His outrage was matched by Nina Drama, who labeled the thought of having ring card boys weird and perverted.

While there is no actual law requiring ring card boys, some European broadcasters and venues push modern equality guidelines, pressuring promotions to display an equal number of ring card girls as ring card boys. Dana White rejected the notion and scrapped them entirely for his show on Saturday.

title: ‘It’s impactful’: Seattle Sports fans see a bright future at stadium gatherings
description: Two major sports events took place in Seattle on Saturday. The Super Bowl-winning Seahawks held their Fan Fest, and the Mariners celebrated 50 years of Seattle baseball as the team hosted the Tampa Bay Rays.
fullText:
Two major sports events took place in Seattle on Saturday. The Super Bowl-winning Seahawks held their Fan Fest, and the Mariners celebrated 50 years of Seattle baseball as the team hosted the Tampa Bay Rays.

Tens of thousands of fans attended both of those events, which took place virtually at the same time, right next to each other.

The sidewalks filled with streams of Seahawks fans with their sights set on Lumen Field, while the baseball faithful headed to T-Mobile Park:

For some fans, the choice between two beloved sports teams wasn't so easy.

"Go 'Hawks, go Mariners baby!" said Preston Erikson, who acknowledged it was impossible for him, his brother and their cousins to attend both. "No, we're not. We wish."

Fans of both teams acknowledged it was a fun problem to have. Seattle boasts a number of top-tier professional men's and women's sports teams, and it won rave reviews for its enthusiasm while hosting six World Cup matches.

"We are a great sports town. I just think- look across the street, you've got Mariners fans, you've got Seahawks fans. It just brings the whole city out. Everyone comes together," said Tijera Loggins.

Trey Erikson told KIRO 7 that there's something special about a sports town and the fans who support their teams.

"We've been in Seattle our whole lives, and it's just something where cultures come together, people come together. It's something words can't even describe. It's emotional. It's important, it's impactful, and it's powerful," he said.

There is an economic impact as well. Local shops and restaurants say business increases every time there's an event at Lumen or T-Mobile.

The economic impact of the World Cup alone here was predicted to be $850 million.

title: Aaron Donald Responds to Rams Return Buzz After Practice Appearance
description: Los Angeles Rams star Aaron Donald is getting closer to coming back, and on Friday, August, he finally spoke about his possible return. The post Aaron Donald Responds to Rams Return Buzz After Practice Appearance appeared first on LA Sports Report.
fullText:
Day by day, Los Angeles Rams star Aaron Donald is getting closer to coming back, and on Friday, August, he finally spoke about his possible return.

Donald has put his head down and focused on his workouts over the past few weeks as he tests himself to see what he can handle.

While the Rams were practicing at Loyola Marymount on Friday, the edge rusher had a workout at UCLA, eventually getting the attention of some fans, and one of them asked if he was coming back to the Rams.

"I don't know yet. We're going to see," the LA legend said.

Donald is only 35 years old, and he retired at 33, looking to go out on top while still playing at a high level.

No doubt, all of the double and triple teams that he faced were starting to wear on him, along with no real goal for him to aim at.

He already delivered LA a Super Bowl, became recognized as the best non-quarterback player in the NFL for years on end, and THE defender of his generation as well.

Donald racked up endless All-Pros and Defensive Player of the Year awards, and when he walked away, there was nothing left.

However, things changed when the Rams traded for Myles Garrett, and all of a sudden, he gets the chance to share the field with a defender just as special as him.

Donald had a workout with the Rams, using their equipment. He did individual drills with Rams defensive line coach Giff Smith, trainer Reggie Scott and strength coach Justin Lovett.

Donald speaks nearly every day with head coach Sean McVay, according to the coach, with an open line of communication.

"He's got such an intentional routine and rhythm. He's taking great care of himself, as we all know," McVay said.

"Getting ready to play football and just working out the way that he has, there's a little bit of a different rhythm and routine."

The Rams and Donald agreed not to decide anything until the team returns to Woodland Hills.

Their first practice at the facility is on Saturday, when McVay will again face questions. At this point, for Rams fans, there is enough smoke to get really excited about Donald returning to wreak havoc in the pocket.

title: EA Sports FC 27: what does the next instalment of the world’s biggest football game have in store?
description:
The all-conquering franchise’s revamps are technically impressive, its transfers more true to life – and its new grassroots social hub is surprising fun
As if the world wasn’t sufficiently football-obsessed, it’s time to prepare for the arrival of its biggest football video game. EA Sports FC 27 (the franchise that used to be Fifa – what better time to no longer be Fifa-branded?) is due to be released on 25 September. I just spent two intense days in Vancouver, where the EA FC games are made, playing FC 27 and talking to its developers.

fullText:
The all-conquering franchise’s revamps are technically impressive, its transfers more true to life – and its new grassroots social hub is surprising fun

As if the world wasn’t sufficiently football-obsessed, it’s time to prepare for the arrival of its biggest football video game. EA Sports FC 27 (the franchise that used to be Fifa – what better time to no longer be Fifa-branded?) is due to be released on 25 September. I just spent two intense days in Vancouver, where the EA FC games are made, playing FC 27 and talking to its developers.

With an annual franchise such as EA FC, it helps to have something fresh to entice regular fans, and FC 27 has a whole new element, entitled the Grounds. It’s a physical hub-type area, similar to the City as seen in 2K’s recent NBA 2K basketball games, but much more pleasant to frequent, split as it is into areas inspired by British, French and Argentinian street-football culture.

The Grounds provides a new physical home for an existing element of EA FC: Clubs, its casual online mode in which you control a single player and play matches closer to kickabouts than real-world football, but beyond that, it has plenty of other activities and distractions.

I spent about an hour in the Grounds, and found it more enjoyable than expected. Among its buildings are playing areas, whose entrances act as lobbies where you can choose to play against random people or to set up a custom game with your FC 27-owning friends. Each playing area hosts a specific type of game, and the Grounds has a map that you can teleport around.

It rewards exploration: I encountered targets that could be smashed by spawning a football and drop-kicking it, some of which were clumped into mini-games. Its games offered clever twists on the Clubs blueprint. In one 3v3 game, target areas appeared for short periods, and if I scored from one, I got a bonus goal for my side. And one game based on dodgeball gave its players three lives, which they would lose if others successfully kicked a ball at them.

The Grounds should prove popular: it has been tastefully and cleverly constructed and will no doubt expand as new game-types are added. You could also envisage it, in future years, hosting a narrative mode along the line of the Journey from Fifa 17 to 19.

FC 26 marked a mission by EA Sports to improve the franchise’s responsiveness by enacting a surprising number of changes to its fundamental gameplay, and that process continues apace in FC 27.

Although anyone who played FC 26 will testify that those efforts actually caused some new problems, such as an annoying tendency for defensive interceptions to bounce back weirdly into the path of forwards. EA Sports, according to gameplay design director Kantcho Doskov, took radical action to eliminate such aberrations: “We had to completely strip out the existing system for interceptions and build a new one from scratch. We spent six months doing that.”

Via a build that let me play Champions League games between a limited number of teams, I found that to be a worthwhile exercise: those defensive bounce-backs were blissfully absent. But an awful lot more was also in evidence in FC 27 on the gameplay revamp front.

Much of this – perhaps counterintuitively at a time when AI is worming its way ever deeper into all our lives – involved paring back the in-game AI. That’s certainly the case for the defensive AI: whereas previously, defenders would rush towards the ball, getting pulled out of position and opening up annoying gaps, FC 27 now gives much more manual control over defensive jockeying, movement and tackles.

Crossing, previously AI-assisted, has been revamped in FC 27, leaving it up to me to get the direction and weight of cross right, then giving me more of a chance to position my centre-forward correctly. The AI controlling forward players, meanwhile, has been improved, so that off-the-ball players now move much more helpfully, allowing pass-and-move sequences, and they are much better at staying onside.

I was also impressed by revamped two-stage corner and free-kick systems. But FC 27, gameplay-wise, achieves what FC 26 set out to, this time with no evident anomalies, and feels more responsive to your inputs than any of its predecessors.

FC 27’s Career Mode, in which you get to play out your fantasies of managing your favourite team, has also been extensively revamped – primarily with a view towards making its transfer system more like the one that operates in the real world, and to force you to do more actual management.

The headline means of doing the latter is called Dynamic OVR. OVR is simply jargon for any player’s all-important overall rating; where previously OVRs remained constant, in FC 27’s Career Mode they will go up and down depending on form, fitness and general happiness. Thus, you will have to rest your best players over the course of a long season, but you may also be able to buy players cheaply with artificially low OVRs if, say, they are coming back from injury.

Pete O’Donnell, FC 27’s Career Mode game director, explains how the game’s transfer system has been modernised: “Previously, you could do things instantly, which was good for a game but was not very realistic. We looked at how clubs interact with each other, how they do the deals themselves, and we spoke to scouts and directors of football. Then it was about extracting the fun bits of those jobs.”

The new system will back you up with more data; now each player will have an xTV (Expected Transfer Value) rating, which should speed negotiations. FC 27 will also reflect clubs’ real-life transfer policies, according to O’Donnell, with clubs’ boards requesting that you sign certain players. Press conferences in FC 27 will force you to make decisions that will please some players and annoy others, and 20 Unexpected Events have been added to Career Mode.

FC 27’s Ultimate Transfer (FUT) mode, the hardcore card-based system that provides a home for most of FC’s loot box action, will have a new headline feature in the form of a Gallery, which will showcase all the players and card-sets collected, rather than just first 11s.

EA Sports says it has also “streamlined” FUT’s previously impenetrable Squad-Based Challenges (SBC) system, and has made a tweak designed to avert stalemates, which affected the latter stages in FUT in FC 26, by restricting plus-level FUT players to three, rather than five, play-styles. But the nature of FUT – which develops over a long period post-launch – means that it will take a while to ascertain whether those changes prove effective.

There will be another major change to FC 27 that has nothing to do with how it plays: because it contains microtransactions, it will now be rated 16+ rather than the previous 3+, after a policy change at age-rating organisation Pegi. Given the game’s enthusiastic young and teenage audience, we asked EA Sports’ top brass to comment, but they blandly responded: “While the game functionally remains the same, this has resulted in a new Pegi age rating. It marks a change in the way we are giving the information to players and parents.”

Beyond Pegi’s European jurisdiction, the game will be rated E for Everybody. But in the UK, parents should think hard about letting youngsters play a 16-rated game. If they are worried about their offspring racking up huge bills for FUT transactions, the good news is that a new Ultimate Plus Edition of the game, which includes loads of stuff that would previously have cost in-game currency, will go on sale. But the bad news is it costs £139.99 and will only be available as a pre-order before 31 August.

title: Lakers Could Add Klay Thompson Following Latest Update

Klay was a mainstay with the Warriors for a very long time, and even when he hit free agency, he chose to sign with the Mavericks rather than join the Lakers, passing up a real chance to join LA.

Recently, Mychal shared that he is "trying" to get Klay to sign with the Lakers, joining Doncic in LA this time and serving as a shooter on the wing.

While Klay is not currently a free agent, he is under contract for one more year, earning $17.4 million. There are rumors of a possible buyout or trade away from the Mavericks, looking to help a team on a contender.

After talk of a buyout, the Mavs reportedly want to instead work out a trade to avoid paying part of Thompson's salary and possibly get any kind of assets.

Thompson, a three-point shooting specialist, has gone through knee and leg injuries that have sapped a good part of his athleticism.

His play was so poor upon his comeback that the Warriors and Thompson made the call to move on.

The Dallas Mavericks, looking to get over the hump in the postseason with Luka Doncic, decided to pursue Thompson and signed him to a big free-agent contract.

However, things changed quickly for the Mavs; they ended up trading Doncic and going through a full rebuild, and they are now led by second-year player Cooper Flagg.

With the Mavs, Thompson has still shot the ball well, though his points have been on a decline, along with his field goal attempts per game.

Last year, he played 69 games, started only eight games, and put up 11.7 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 1.4 assists.

Thompson, one of the greatest shooters of all time, shot 39.1% in 2024 and 38.3% last year from deep.

The Lakers need help on the wings, and a change of scenery, alongside an established role on a competitor, could be what Thompson needs to get his career going again.

At 36 and with so many surgeries, he may not have much juice left, but if he does, the Lakers could use him.

LA may be more willing to sign him following a buyout rather than trade for him, but they will likely be inquiring to see how viable adding Thompson is.

title: ‘Sold the game’: Criticism rises against Caitlin Clark after she gets ‘punked’ to lose game

The Indiana Fever are doing their best to keep the focus on basketball, following weeks of controversy tied to comments reserve guard Sophie Cunningham made about transgender athletes participating in women's sports. "There is so much good going on in the WNBA. I think basketball is being played at the highest level it's ever been," Cunningham told WISH-TV News in Indianapolis. "There's just so much distraction. The WNBA media, all we ever do is cover everything except basketball. It's like, what are we doing? You can talk about other things; I think those are great stories. It shows fans who people are outside of the court, but I also think we gotta keep the main thing the main thing."

"I want to get back to basketball; it's always been about basketball," she insisted. "That interview happened in February when I was asked a question. And for me, I just want to make sure the focus stays where it should."

The Fever faced off against the Las Vegas Aces on Thursday, and although the team may be working on eliminating distractions as the playoffs draw nearer, one player was clearly off her A game. Clark finished the game with 20 points and 8 assists, but struggled immensely with her efficiency, shooting 7-for-20 from the field, including 2-for-10 from the three-point line. "Caitlin Clark choke job," one fan wrote.

"Caitlin Clark sold the f*cking game with the dumb*ss missed two FTs! Trash!!!" someone else added.

Clark then had the game-losing turnover, as it led to a buzzer-beater game-winning three-pointer by Aces point guard Chelsea Gray.

"Aja Wilson just punked Caitlin Clark for game," one fan put bluntly.

Even though it wasn't her best outing, Clark managed to leave a massive impact on the game. If this is her floor, the Fever franchise is in extremely good shape.

title: Is Dana White right? Why fight sports is — and has to be — about more than just 'holy s***' moments
description: White continues to emphasize the value of 'holy s***' moments for both the UFC and his Power Slap brand. But isn't fight sports about more than just social media clips?
fullText:
A few times lately, UFC CEO Dana White has offered the same succinct description of his own job.

"I sell holy s*** moments for a living," White said on a podcast a while back. This was while extolling the virtues of Power Slap, which he insisted will one day be bigger than the UFC in part because of its consistent delivery of those moments. (More on this in a moment.)

He alluded to it again just last week, at the pre-fight press conference for the UFC Fight Night event in Belgrade, Serbia. When he was asked which fight he was most looking forward to, White first called it a "s***** question" and then eventually replied that he was simply hoping for "a few holy s*** moments on Saturday night."

The fighters did their best to deliver. Out of 14 fights on the card, 10 ended in the first round — a record for the UFC's modern era. But then, if quick finishes is all you're after, you can usually get that just by booking a series of mismatches. Take some guy who has no business being in the Octagon, throw him in against a gifted purveyor of sanctioned violence, and you'll probably get a moment or two of memorable human carnage, at least there at the end.

It's an interesting way to think about the sport, though. Moments. Not whole fights. Not personalities or individual stories or even the vaguely mathematical logic of the rankings. Just big, crazy moments that will have Joe Rogan making that face as he grabs a fistful of Jon Anik's shirt.

Maybe this is just what it takes to adapt to the social media age. Spreading the gospel of the sport means you need clips, those little bite-sized reels you can post to Instagram or TikTok, sneaking into people's algorithms whether they like it or not.

This seems to be the entire goal with the Power Slap venture. Every time it comes up, which is to say when White brings it up on podcasts and in interviews, he spotlights its success on social media. The follower count. The number of total views per month. Every time a set of eyes falls upon a short video of some Power Slapper clubbing a stationary human target, that serves as proof to White that his side quest is working.

Behold, the massive popularity of people slapping other people who just have to stand there and take it. It doesn't matter if no one can name a single Power Slap star or recall specific, what, matches? Bouts? It's a machine for moments, according to White, and moments are what he's selling.

"This will be bigger than the UFC," White told the Trigger Nometry podcast. "You don't have to train 10 years and be an incredible athlete to do it."

In other words, any jabroni off the street could show up and give you a moment. Not like this MMA thing, which requires boring stuff like discipline and skill and training and athleticism. This is even better, White said, because "you might have a whole night of [MMA] fights and not have your holy s*** moment; Power Slap is one, two, holy s***."

First of all, imagine being a professional MMA fighter, having dedicated your life to this sport and sacrificed a ton to get to the UFC level, and then hearing the boss say that the untrained, unathletic slappers are better because they create more clip-worthy moments.

But second, from a fan perspective, what do those moments really mean? What kind of staying power do they have if I don't care about the people involved or understand some larger context for the whole thing?

Think about one of the biggest moments in UFC history: Forrest Griffin vs. Stephan Bonnar at the very first finale event for "The Ultimate Fighter" back in 2005. That fight was practically nothing but 'holy s***' moments, but what elevated it to great sports drama was the story behind it. The winner got the big UFC contract. His dream would come true. So when you saw them fighting like two stray dogs battling over the last chicken wing, you understood what it meant and why it mattered.

Moments are great for highlight reels. They fit right in among the junk food content scroll on social media. But I question their ability to make someone a fan — or to hold onto them beyond the time it takes to flick their thumb in the direction of the little heart button.

The thing that makes fighting unlike any other sport is its ability to create anticipation and urgency leading to an inevitable and unpredictable payoff. Two people want the same thing. Only one can have it. They both say the prize will be theirs. Saturday night we're going to lock them in a cage and find out, whether it takes 10 seconds or 25 minutes.

The appeal goes beyond just one crazy moment. It has to. Because if not, why would I sit through an entire UFC event? Especially when I could just hang out on Instagram and wait for the 15 seconds that matter to come and find me.

title: ‘LeBron, do you have any desire to be a woman?’: Donald Trump reveals plans as WNBA coach
description: Donald Trump has felt strongly about basketball as of late. fullText:
Donald Trump has felt strongly about basketball as of late. The President recently weighed in on one of the longest-lasting debates going on in sports circles: who the greatest basketball player of all time is. While it's widely viewed as a two-horse race between Michael Jordan and LeBron James, Trump made it clear that for him, it's a fairly easy choice.

"Well, Michael Jordan is a guy that's a friend of mine. He's a really good guy," Trump said during a press conference following James' decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers for his 24th season in the NBA. "And I think LeBron… Maybe he's a racist, but maybe he doesn't like Trump. I don't know. I only like people that like me, so I would say Michael Jordan all the way."

The NBA isn't the only basketball league the President has been following, either. White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt revealed that the President has been following the controversy surrounding WNBA guard Sophie Cunningham of the Indiana Fever, who sparked debate when she said in a profile that she thinks it's important to keep transgender girls from competing in the same sports as other girls.

"I don't believe he (President Trump) has reached out to her. I know he is following the story. As you know, this is something the president feels strongly about as well, and the American people do, too: that men should not be playing in women's sports," Leavitt said.

"It's completely ludicrous that anyone could support that. It's even more ludicrous you have Sophie Cunningham, a female athlete herself, very accomplished in her own right, coming forth and speaking that truth that men shouldn't play in women's sports — we want to protect women and girls — and the backlash she is receiving from Democrats and left-wing fingers across the country is astonishing. They are clearly very out of touch with the American public on this issue."

Now, the President has linked his James-Jordan feelings and his take on trans athletes in the WNBA.

"I'd be the greatest women's basketball coach in history because I don't like LeBron James," Trump said in a public address, "I like Michael Jordan much better. But I'd go up to LeBron James.

“I’d be the greatest women’s basketball coach in history. I don’t like LeBron James, I like Michael Jordan much better. But, I’d go up to LeBron James…I’d say, ‘LeBron, did you ever have any desire to be a woman? Because what I’d love you to do is star on my team.” pic.twitter.com/xU5lt6hPeH

"It doesn't matter, I'd say, 'LeBron, did you ever have any desire to be a woman? Because what I'd love you to do is star on my team that I'm building up.' I will have the greatest team in history. They'll never lose. Nobody will come within 70 points of this team. Now, we have to change that, and we have to make it okay to talk about it."

It's an odd thing to say considering that the WNBA doesn't have a single transgender player in it, and no transgender athletes are dominating at the highest levels of college basketball either. The one transgender female basketball player that anti-trans advocates have used as an example recently, Julien Tetart, hasn't even reached the highest level of professional basketball in France

title: GB Snowsport loses UK Sport funding but athletes unaffected
description: UK Sport will no longer channel investment in skiing and snowboarding through the sports' UK governing body, GB Snowsport.
fullText:
UK Sport will no longer channel investment in skiing and snowboarding through the sports' UK governing body, GB Snowsport.

It will instead find a new way to deliver £12.5m of funding to athletes and coaches before the 2030 Winter Olympics and Paralympics.

The news comes six months after Team GB enjoyed their most successful Winter Olympics at Milan-Cortina.

They won five medals, including an unprecedented three golds, one of which was in the snowboard cross mixed team event - a first ever gold medal on snow.

UK Sport has written to all snowsport athletes who receive funding to make them aware of the decision, also confirming funding grants will continue to be paid directly. An independent review will now be set up into the governance of GBS.

The funding is part of a record investment of more than £33m into winter sports for the four-year cycle.

Kate Baker, director of performance and people at UK Sport, said: "Competition across Olympic and Paralympic winter sport is only getting stronger, which is why it's more important than ever that we invest where we can have the biggest impact.

"It is also why we are not afraid of driving the change needed to give our athletes the very best chance of success."

In a statement, GBS said it was "disappointed" by the decision but will continue to work with UK Sport. However, it said it "reserves the right to keep all options open to ensure that the achievements of the past four years are not lost".

GB Snowsport has changed its chair twice in the past three years and is currently advertising for a new chair.

Michael Oesterlin, who has been a non-executive director at the organisation for four years, is interim chair.

The GBS statement added: "We have recently concluded an independent governance review funded by UK Sport, which has confirmed that our governance standards remain strong and appropriate.

"We look forward to engaging fully and robustly in any new review, which we are confident will reach the same conclusions."

The increased overall investment is up from about £32.5m for the 2026 Winter Olympics and Paralympics cycle.

It was the third time in four Winter Olympics that Team GB had won five medals, but they had only ever won a maximum of one gold medal on the previous occasions. ParalympicsGB returned with one silver medal.

The next Games will be held in the French Alps in 2030.

Baker added the results "showed what British winter sport is capable of, with incredible performances across more sports than ever before".

"With another Winter Games on European soil and an incredibly talented crop of athletes, we're excited by what's possible over the next four years," she added.

From the investment announcement, about a third (£10m) will go to bobsleigh and skeleton, which provided two of Team GB's three gold medals at Milan-Cortina.

Other sports benefiting are curling (£6.54m), wheelchair curling (£1.93m), ice skating (£2m) and ice hockey which will receive £445,000 in 'transition funding' which Tim Bratton, interim chief executive of Ice Hockey UK, says will be used to "transition into a self-sustainable governing body for our fantastic sport".

From 2030, funding for bobsleigh and skeleton programmes from UK Sport will be operated by a new "multi-sport delivery organisation" called Sport Org which will operate elite performance programmes on behalf of governing bodies.

Sport Org already oversees curling and wheelchair curling programmes and will take over from the British Bobsleigh & Skeleton Association (BBSA) in the run-up to Utah 2034.

title: Today’s Papers: Milan mourns Baresi, Leão U-turn and Inter close on Romero

fullText:
Italian football pauses on Tuesday to say goodbye to Franco Baresi, and the country's three sports dailies devote their front pages both to his funeral and to a transfer market showing no sign of slowing.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, Corriere dello Sport and Tuttosport alike, the day belongs to Baresi.

His funeral takes place at 11am at Milan's Basilica of Sant'Ambrogio, where thousands of supporters are expected.

Under headlines including "Per sempre libero" and "Tutto il mondo per salutare Baresi," the papers report that former team-mates from Paolo Maldini and Marco van Basten to Dejan Savićević and Roberto Donadoni will join Milan owner Gerry Cardinale, president Paolo Scaroni and Inter counterpart Beppe Marotta, with delegations from Real Madrid and Barcelona also present.

Milan's first team, on tour in Australia, will be represented only by the injured Christian Pulisic and Santiago Giménez, and will wear black armbands for Wednesday's friendly against Inter in Perth.

The market, though, presses on.

Gazzetta leads with "Giravolta Leao," reporting that Rafael Leão's expected Milan exit is no longer certain: with no concrete offers arriving, the Portugal forward is now working to stay and win back his place under Rúben Amorim.

The pink paper also trumpets Juventus's spending, already €138m, it notes, on the likes of Kerim Alajbegović and Randal Kolo Muani, and Como's capture of Chelsea's Trevoh Chalobah, billed as "another Champions-level signing."

Corriere dello Sport leads on a goalkeeping tangle it dubs "Intrigo Suzuki," with Parma's Zion Suzuki courted by PSG and Juventus exploring a loan move for a keeper as Luciano Spalletti also eyes Guglielmo Vicario.

Its main splash, though, is Cristian Romero: Tottenham are said to be willing to let the Argentine leave for €40m, but his salary and the need for an Inter sale first complicate a deal that Piero Ausilio continues to push.

Tuttosport frames Juventus's attacking business as a "last call," reporting talks with Atlético Madrid over a possible exchange involving Alexander Sørloth and Nico González, the Norwegian said to be ready for Italy, the Argentine keen to stay in Spain.

The Turin paper agrees Inter's pursuit of Romero, alongside Moussa Diaby, is well advanced, declaring the "Cuti" deal all but done.

Off the pitch, Corriere tracks FIFA's fallout: with UEFA threatening legal action after the abandoned World Cup sell-off, it reports that Gianni Infantino has turned to his ally Donald Trump for support, while Concacaf's Victor Montagliani is floated as a possible successor.

title: Sky Sports: Liverpool to miss out on transfer targe as rivals reach agreement
description: Ayyoub Bouaddi to Manchester City latest leaves Liverpool weighing Trey Nyoni optionManchester City are moving into a strong position in the race for Ayyoub Bouaddi, with Sky Sports reporter Florian P...
fullText:
Manchester City are moving into a strong position in the race for Ayyoub Bouaddi, with Sky Sports reporter Florian Plettenberg reporting that the Lille midfielder "has reached a full verbal agreement" with the Premier League club. Negotiations with Lille are still continuing, and other sides remain attentive, but the direction of travel appears increasingly clear.

For Liverpool, this looks like one of those situations where admiration and action have not aligned. Bouaddi had been viewed as a player of interest in recruitment circles, yet interest alone does not complete a deal, particularly when the financials begin to escalate. The figures now being discussed around the Moroccan international are significant, with estimates around £85m placing the move firmly into premium territory.

That matters because Liverpool's transfer window cannot be viewed through one signing in isolation. Squad planning under Andoni Iraola requires balance, and there are multiple areas still under assessment before the new campaign begins. Committing that level of outlay to one midfield addition would inevitably shape the rest of the summer, especially if Liverpool are also exploring other high-cost attacking options such as Bradley Barcola.

From a recruitment perspective, there is logic in stepping back when valuations move beyond a club's comfort zone. Bouaddi is highly regarded and clearly attracting major interest, but Liverpool do not appear prepared to be dragged into an inflated battle if it compromises wider business. That is a strategic call, not necessarily a reflection on the player.

Timing is also important here. Liverpool have spent pre-season assessing internal solutions, and Trey Nyoni has done his chances no harm at all. His display against Leeds United offered another reminder of his technical quality and growing authority in midfield. He played a central role in the move that led to Florian Wirtz's goal, switching play superbly to Jeremie Frimpong before the final ball arrived.

Perhaps more telling was the change in Liverpool's midfield after Nyoni went off at half-time. The structure looked less secure and the fluency dipped, which only added weight to the impression he is becoming a serious option in Iraola's plans. That does not mean he and Bouaddi are direct comparisons, but it does strengthen the case for trusting what is already emerging at Kirkby.

If Liverpool are working within tighter financial parameters than in previous windows, decisions like this become easier to understand. Passing on an £85m midfielder may create room to address several needs rather than one. Bouaddi may yet prove worth every penny at Manchester City, but Liverpool's approach suggests they are prioritising flexibility, value and squad-wide improvement over a headline purchase.

In that context, Nyoni's rise could become more than a promising subplot. It may help shape the whole window.

As a disappointed Liverpool supporter, this report is frustrating even if it makes sense on paper. Bouaddi looks like exactly the sort of elite young midfielder top clubs should be fighting for, and hearing that Manchester City are close to getting him while Liverpool stand aside never sits well. Supporters can accept missing out on a player, but it becomes harder to take when a direct rival appears ready to strengthen without the same hesitation.

There is a wider concern too. Liverpool cannot keep leaning on the idea that internal development will solve every squad issue. Trey Nyoni has looked excellent and deserves enormous credit, but expecting a 19-year-old to carry such responsibility across a long season feels unfair. Young players should be supported, not used as the reason to avoid major investment.

If the price really is around £85m, then caution is understandable. Still, elite midfielders cost elite money, and Liverpool know that better than most. The concern from a fan perspective is that this starts to look like another summer of careful explanations rather than decisive action. Bouaddi may have been expensive, but watching Manchester City add another top talent while Liverpool talk themselves out of it is difficult to dress up as anything other than a disappointment.

fullText:
Michael Mahon, Ph.D., is eager and excited about returning to his alma mater as the athletic director at Scranton Prep.

Mahon, a former teacher, principal, superintendent, higher education administrator, and coach, replaces Grey Simpson, who resigned after the season and will be a teacher and coach at Woodberry Forest School in Virginia, the school announced in a press release on Monday.

A 1986 graduate of Scranton Prep, Mahon excelled as a football player and catcher for the baseball team. He helped lead the Cavaliers to a District 2 Class 3A championship and a first-round playoff game against Montoursville and its pitching ace, Mike Mussina.

In college, Mahon played and coached baseball at the University of Scranton. He started his professional career as a science teacher at Scranton Prep, also served as a coach at the high school level, and then embarked on a long career in administration.

Mahon earned a Bachelor of Science in Secondary Education and a Master of Science in School Administration from the University of Scranton, a Ph.D. in Human Development with a concentration in Administration from Marywood University, and an M.B.A. from the University of Massachusetts Amherst.

“This is 30 years after I left as a teacher and 40 years after I left as a student, so to return to Scranton Prep, my alma mater, is exciting,” Mahon, 58, said. “When this opportunity came up, I reflected and realized that one of the most enjoyable aspects of my career was when I was teaching and coaching. It occurred to me that it would be so much fun.

“Scranton Prep has a very long and storied history of athletic success and a tradition of a strong Jesuit education, which both are priorities for me in my life and brought me back. The thought of being able to go back and work as part of a team with the leadership of President Rev. A.J. Rizzo, S.J., and Principal Kris Cupillari, and have the opportunity to reengage in things that I have enjoyed is truly something that I am looking forward to.”

While a student at the University of Scranton, Mahon started his coaching career as part of Phil Angeli’s staff. He was an assistant freshman coach for the Cavaliers. That experience, he noted, is what inspired him to go into teaching and coaching.

Mahon played baseball for the University of Scranton, where he graduated with a degree in secondary education and a master’s degree in school administration. He continued coaching as an assistant for the late Bill Howerton at the University of Scranton. He was also a head varsity baseball coach at Abington Heights in 1997, then moved into school administration.

After leaving coaching, Mahon started as an assistant principal at Wyalusing, then was an assistant principal at Pleasant Valley. He became the high school principal at Bangor before accepting the superintendent job at Wyalusing.

Mahon returned to Northeastern Pennsylvania and became the superintendent at Abington Heights, where he spent 17 years. He moved on to be superintendent at Southern Lehigh before accepting his position at The Wright Center in 2025.

As Athletic Director, Mahon will provide leadership for Scranton Prep’s athletic programs, supporting coaches and student-athletes while building upon the school’s longstanding tradition of excellence in athletics and education, the school cited in the press release.

“I’ve been closely connected to high school sports as an administrator and superintendent, and I have watched the developments and changes,” Mahon said. “Yes, things have changed, but the core values of discipline, leadership and dedication remain the same. I am looking forward to getting back into it.”

title: Why the Commonwealth Games are important to NI athletes
description:
The slimmed down version of the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow are over and Northern Ireland athletes will return home with 16 medals.
It's the second biggest haul in history, behind only the 18 won in Birmingham four years ago but this time with fewer sports.
But why are the Commonwealth Games so important to athletes from Northern Ireland, especially in the bigger sporting picture?
fullText:
The slimmed-down version of the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow is over and Northern Ireland athletes will return home with 16 medals.

It's the second-biggest haul in history, behind only the 18 won in Birmingham four years ago but this time with fewer sports.

The build-up to the 2026 Games had been dominated by a change of host, a scaled-down schedule and a number of big-name withdrawals.

Yet, after 10 days of competition in Scotland, the performances leave the lasting impression.

But why are the Commonwealth Games so important to athletes from Northern Ireland, especially in the bigger sporting picture?

McKeown and Kelly win men's pairs gold after tiebreak

From Love Island to Commonwealth gold for McConnell

Milestone moment for O'Connor with Glasgow gold

The Commonwealth Games fall at the halfway point of the Olympic cycle and, in the case of Glasgow, just months before qualification in many sports gets underway for Los Angeles 2028.

It's an opportunity to take stock of where you are as an athlete moving forward, or for young athletes to gain a first experience of a multi-sport event.

The Commonwealth Games have always been an important bridge to greater things.

Lady Mary Peters won Commonwealth medals before the Olympic pentathlon title in 1972, while boxers Wayne McCullough and Aidan Walsh also became Commonwealth medallists before they stood on an Olympic podium.

More recently, Rhys McClenaghan's first major title on the pommel horse was a Commonwealth gold in 2018. Meanwhile, four years ago swimmer Daniel Wiffen won a silver medal at the Commonwealths.

Both men are now Olympic and world champions.

Northern Ireland's golden girl in Glasgow, Kate O'Connor, was a silver medallist from four years ago and went on to finish second at the World Championships in-between Games.

This was her third Commonwealths having competed as a 17-year-old in the Gold Coast in 2018, and she says the competition "has been so good to me".

"Having that opportunity whenever I was a 17-year-old to travel across the world and compete against senior athletes on an international stage, and compete against that many people, not many 17-year-olds get that experience," O'Connor told BBC Sport NI.

"Then in 2022 and I was in with a chance of a medal, I'd had that experience from the previous Games."

O'Connor said that winning gold in Glasgow was part of her journey, and charted her progress from a junior athlete into regular medal contention on the world stage.

"This year I was in a really privileged position where I'd come in and I was the favourite, but that obviously comes with its own pressures and I think I navigated it very well.

"I'm really proud of how I managed to deal with the last three Games and how I've grown as an athlete.

"The Games have definitely stood to me. I'm so thankful that I've had the opportunity to compete in them."

The Commonwealth Games also has its own progression pathway.

The boxing team produced six medals, another impressive haul from a much less experienced team than in recent editions of the Games.

Jon McConnell, 23, is now Commonwealth champion, defending the title won last time by Aidan Walsh.

Can he now go on to win an Olympic medal like Walsh did? He might, if he stays off Love Island….

Kaci Rock is also 23 and a silver medallist and is already looking ahead to Olympic qualification.

"I've such a hunger now to move forward and the next big thing is the Olympics in Los Angeles and I'm going to do everything I can to get there. I've stood on the podium at the Commonwealth Games and now I want to stand out he podium at the Olympics," she said.

Swimmer Ellie McCartney won a magnificent bronze medal in the 100m breaststroke.

Three years ago, the Enniskillen swimmer's potential was noticed after winning two golds at the Youth Commonwealth Games.

Since then the 21-year-old has reached a first senior world final and taken a medal in Glasgow.

There were other notable achievements from some of the youngest members of Team NI and, like O'Connor, this experience will hopefully help them in the future.

Athlete Nick Griggs was sixth in the final of the men's 5000m while in the pool, 16-year-old Emily Hughes, the youngest member of Team NI, was a member of the 4x100m freestyle relay squad that set a new Irish Senior record.

A pair of 18-year-olds, Matthew Hamilton and Adam Bradley, also set Irish Junior records.

Another athlete waiting on A-Level results, weightlifter Harrison McGrogan, was fifth.

Then there was the emotion. The scream that judoka Rachael Hawkes let out on winning bronze after losing the same fight four years ago was almost primal, it meant so much to her.

There were the tears of bowler Chloe Wilson after winning bronze with Shauna O'Neill in the women's pairs.

Wilson, 23, and O'Neill, 26, have put to bed forever the myth that bowls is only played by pensioners.

Winning a medal is one thing but doing it with your best friend is something special.

"Words can't even describe how much it means. Just to be standing up there with Shauna, it's something really special," Wilson said with tears in her eyes.

O'Neill said the moment "is going to live with me for the rest of my life".

Gary Kelly had won bronze in the men's singles bowls in Delhi in 2010 and a silver four years ago.

In Glasgow it was another bronze in the singles but that elusive gold would finally come in the men's pairs with Adam McKeown, himself now a two-time Commonwealth Games champion.

Bowls isn't an Olympic sport so the Commonwealth Games is the pinnacle.

"The Commonwealth Games is the biggest opportunity for us, for media exposure, and for people that maybe wouldn't normally view our game and our sport," said Kelly

"It's incredibly important, and it's been fantastic for it to be part of this and for it to be respected as one of the six core sports of the Commonwealth Games. I think it deserves that."

Chef de Mission of Northern Ireland, Conal Heatley, believes strongly that the Commonwealth Games have prepared athletes for future successes.

"It was a very important part of their program," Heatley said on the 65 NI athletes in Glasgow.

"Whether it's Commonwealth Games, that's their pinnacle, or whether they will look to go on to Olympics, but each and every one of them strove to do their best here for Team NI."

The Indian city of Ahmedabad has already been announced as hosts for 2030.

Two years ago the future of the Commonwealth Games was uncertain when Victoria in Australia pulled out of hosting.

Glasgow stepped in, and while smaller and cheaper, they've provided competitive sport and enjoyment for spectators and athletes alike.

History shows how important the Commonwealth Games have been for athletes from Northern Ireland in building for the future while still winning medals at this level.

"Many, many of our athletes who have gone on to win Olympic medals have come through Commonwealth Games," Heatley added.

"It gives them an incredible opportunity to gain experience and prepare for the future."

title: Today’s Papers – Italy pays tribute to Baresi
description: Italian football is in mourning, and on Saturday its three great sports dailies handed their front pages over entirely to Franco Baresi, the Milan and Italy legend who died on Friday aged 66.According...
fullText:
Italian football is in mourning, and on Saturday its three great sports dailies handed their front pages over entirely to Franco Baresi, the Milan and Italy legend who died on Friday aged 66.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, the country has lost “a giant.” Beneath a photograph of Baresi lifting the European Cup, the pink paper leads with “Mio Capitano”, “My Captain”, recalling how the boy nicknamed “il Piscinin” grew into a colossus who won everything and stood by his Milan even through their relegation to Serie B.

Inside, tributes and interviews pour in from those who knew him best, among them former coach Fabio Capello, ex-team-mate Christian Panucci and Rossoneri great Gianni Rivera, alongside columns from the likes of Luigi Garlando and Beppe Bergomi.

Corriere dello Sport: Strikes a similar chord with “6 per sempre”, “Six forever”, a nod to the shirt number Milan retired in his honour. Under the line “Addio capitano,” the paper hails “elegance become legend” and reports that Italian football is “in tears,” having “lost a beat of our heart.”

It traces the arc of a life defined by 21 trophies, from the 1982 World Cup to three European Cups under Arrigo Sacchi and Fabio Capello, and carries the words of long-time defensive partner Alessandro Costacurta, who recalled how Baresi “knew how to lead you through his conduct.”

Turin’s Tuttosport keeps it simple: “Un capitano,” above the dates 1960-2026 and another image of Baresi and the European Cup. Its tributes reach beyond the trophies to the moments that defined the man, the courage of his tearful stand at Pasadena in the 1994 World Cup final, and the 39 red roses he laid in memory of the Heysel victims, “from a champion of humanity.”

The papers also carry the details of a nation’s farewell. Baresi’s funeral will be held on Tuesday 4 August at 11am at the Basilica of Sant’Ambrogio in Milan, with the Rossoneri squad unable to attend as they are away on their pre-season tour. FIGC president Giovanni Malagò has ordered a minute’s silence before every friendly played in Italy this weekend.

title: Stephen A. Smith on Fauci: ‘You can’t show up on Capitol Hill and plead the Fifth 111 times’
description: Sports commentator Stephen A. Smith said Thursday that former White House chief medical adviser Anthony Fauci should have answered lawmakers’ questions during the hostile Senate hearing earlier this w...
fullText:
Sports commentator Stephen A. Smith said Thursday that former White House chief medical adviser Anthony Fauci should have answered lawmakers' questions during the hostile Senate hearing earlier this week instead of invoking his Fifth Amendment rights.

Smith argued that Fauci owed the public an explanation after serving as the face of the nation's COVID-19 response.

"As it strictly pertains to the coronavirus pandemic, my attitude is, with you being the face that you have been, you can't show up on Capitol Hill and plead the Fifth 111 times," he told NewsNation's Chris Cuomo. "You just can't do that. That's not right. You've got to answer some questions."

During a three-hour hearing before the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee on Wednesday, Fauci pleaded the Fifth 111 times as Republicans blasted him over his handling of the pandemic and accused the doctor of covering up the U.S.'s involvement in gain-of-function research that could have caused the spread of the virus.

Smith acknowledged that Fauci, who led the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases for nearly 40 years, may have had a legitimate legal reason to remain silent — pointing to a pardon he received from former President Biden on his final day in office for potential offenses between Jan. 1, 2014, and Jan. 19, 2025.

"Anything that he said clearly could potentially incriminate him and could give them fodder to come after him for future potential transgressions, and they can go after him that way, and I certainly don't want an 85-year-old man thrown in jail, particularly with his exemplary service," the commentator told NewsNation.

During the hearing, Republicans argued Fauci had no basis to invoke the Fifth Amendment, when the doctor continuously repeated his one-line phrase: "On the advice of counsel, I respectfully decline to answer based upon my rights under the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution."

Before the hearing, committee Chair Rand Paul (R-Ky.) released more than 1,000 pages of Fauci's personal diary and work records. Fauci condemned the move as an attempt at "embarrassing and intimidating" him.

Paul, who has sought to indict Fauci, is also threatening to hold him in contempt after the hearing.

While Democrats praised the doctor for his decades of public service and leadership in the infectious disease space, many Republicans accused him of being responsible for COVID-19-related deaths, vaccine injuries and destroying the American public's trust in the healthcare system.
