title: Rugby v cricket - England's George swaps sports to help tackle MND
description: England and Saracens' Jamie George on why he and Somerset's Lewis Gregory are playing a charity cricket match to raise money for motor neurone disease charities.
fullText:
Rugby might be England and Saracens hooker Jamie George's first love but cricket is still a regular part of his sporting life and career.

It's why he and his club team-mates did not need much persuading to 

"We [Saracens] do play [cricket] - our warm-up [for] every rugby session - summer, winter, snowing, rain - is one hand, one bounce," George told BBC Radio Somerset.

"The boys love it because they're mad-keen cricket fans."

George will skipper 'Team Rugby' for the game on 19 August at the County Ground in Taunton, in a side that also includes current and former England internationals Owen Farrell, Elliot Daly, Ben Earl and Max Malins.

Somerset captain Lewis Gregory will lead the opposition to tie in with his testimonial year, with Surrey and England's Jamie Overton and former Somerset all-rounder Peter Trego also on the teamsheet.

George was in the stand at the County Ground for a T20 match earlier this season and bumped into Somerset all-rounder Tom Kohler-Cadmore, who was injured at the time, and the idea was touted.

"I'm actually doing a testimonial year next year and I said the dream would be to play a game of cricket somewhere like this," George, who captained England during this summer's Nations Series, said.

"[Kohler-Cadmore] said: 'Why don't we do it for Lewis' testimonial?' I thought it's an unbelievable opportunity."

Back with his Saracens team, George instantly started pulling a side together.

"We were out to dinner and within seconds we were coming up with a batting order," he said.

"I suggested we should merge teams and they said 'no, we want to take them on', categorically rugby versus cricket."

While George and his team-mates are not short of experience, with hundreds of international caps and English Prem games between them, on the cricket pitch it is, of course, a different story compared to their opponents.

However, the rugby squad do have some experience to call upon.

Daly represented Surrey as a teenager and played for England at age-grade level, while Earl similarly played for Kent as an under-15.

"They're both very handy so at least we'll get some runs on the board and then we'll have to scramble around a bit," George, 35, said.

As for what kind of player George will be? "Like a Daren Sammy [former West Indies T20 World Cup-winning captain] type role, I would not bowl and I'd bat at nine or 10 and just be there for morale," he said.

"I'm an old man now but I used to play a lot of cricket back when I was at school."

Gregory, who is Somerset's all-time leading T20 wicket-taker, is happy the game is being played on his turf rather than the other way around and in a rugby match.

"A lot of our lads are excited to see the rugby boys in action and it will be nice to put them under a bit of pressure rather than it being in a rugby game, because that could be a little bit messy," he said.

The decision to support the MND Association was also an easy one for both Gregory and George, with former players in both rugby and cricket having been diagnosed with the disease in recent years.

MND is a neurological condition which affects the brain and spinal cord, and can affect a person's ability to talk, walk and breathe.

Former England and Gloucestershire fast bowler David 'Syd' Lawrence died in 2025, having been diagnosed with MND the year previously.

Doddie Weir, the former Scotland lock, died in 2022, six years after being diagnosed with MND, and having raised millions of pounds and awareness to combat the disease, while former Gloucester lock Ed Slater and former England captain Lewis Moody both live with MND.

"It's a horrible disease and that's why the rugby and the cricket communities are very similar, there's a lot of crossover between the two," George said.

"We look after our own and we want to try to do everything we can to raise as much awareness and hopefully find a cure."

title: Can boxing ‘addiction’ ever be cured? Pain of retiring explored in new Sky documentary
description: IN FOCUS: Alex Pattle dives into the Sky Sports film ‘The Final Round’ and speaks to champion turned pundit Johnny Nelson, a key voice in the documentary
fullText:
Sky Sports’s new documentary is stacked with sobering soundbites. In one scene, boxing coach Joe Gallagher recalls hearing a mother ask her son: “Are all the lows worth that one high?” The answer, of course, was “yes”. As Gallagher puts it: “Everyone wants their own Rocky story.”

But as Sky explores, that doesn’t always mean a rousing underdog story. Rocky’s sequels showed Sylvester Stallone’s character struggling with retirement, and this is the premise of The Final Round.

Releasing on Friday, the film features interviews with former world champions like Johnny Nelson and Josh Warrington, while Gallagher and Dominic Ingle are among the coaches to speak, promoter Eddie Hearn features, and commentator Andy Clarke weaves together themes of “addiction”, sacrifice, and ego.

The documentary even includes one of the final interviews with the late, great Ricky Hatton, whose internal fights after retiring matched any that he had in the ring.

Many boxers tell themselves, “‘I’ve got one more good fight in me,’” Hatton says. “Nine times out of 10, you haven’t. That was the case with me.”

Indeed, in 2022, a 42-year-old Hatton boxed Marco Antonio Barrera in an exhibition, and he was even due for another before his untimely death last September.

“Ego never leaves a fighter, and that’s the problem,” Nelson says. It outlasts the “fire”, he adds, shrewdly touching on an unfair fight between the two emotions.

Yet it’s not just about fire and ego; a question of identity arises, as does a fear of life post-boxing. Retirement is “frightening”, says heavyweight veteran Dave Allen, who reversed his own exit from the sport. “Apart from ‘Dad’, I’m just a boxer. I’m not even David, the normal human being.”

Warrington, whose boxing future is up in the air at the time of writing, explains: “I wake up on fight day and it’s like everything’s brighter, everything smells better, I’m more alert... that’s an unreal feeling.” And then the kicker: “Once that stops, you’ll never feel it again.”

Does this explain Tyson Fury’s five false retirements? Perhaps. They get their own spotlight in the documentary, as do comebacks that occur decades after retirement: for example, a 58-year-old Mike Tyson facing a 27-year-old YouTuber, Jake Paul, in 2024.

The film touches on how boxers don’t just miss the buzz of fight night, but also the camaraderie of their gyms, while the financial turmoil that has afflicted many fighters gets significant screen time.

Most boxers need a second job, and promoter and manager Steve Wood explains: “Ninety per cent of the fighters I look after are not earning enough to pay tax. I’ve had a couple of world champions; they’re the only two likely to be able to retire comfortably.”

In an interview with The Independent, Nelson touches on all of these topics, as well as his plans to create a proper pension scheme for boxers – something his own promoter, Eddie’s father Barry Hearn, attempted unsuccessfully.

Barry tried putting a small percentage of boxers’ purses towards a pension, but fighters’ distrust and/or short-term thinking thwarted the plan. Nelson, who toyed with his own comeback nine years after retiring, reflects on receiving a £97,000 pension from Hearn several years ago, inspiring the 59-year-old.

Nelson wants to create a scheme that would pay £2,000 into a pension for each boxer every year, as long as the fighter competes two to three times annually and puts 5 per cent of their purse into the same pension – with the money coming from a combination of TV companies, government grants, and private sponsorship. Nelson has spoken to the British Boxing Board of Control, figures in parliament, Scottish Widows, and potential financiers while trying to get the scheme off the ground.

“If I was a parent and my son wanted to box, I wouldn’t want him to box for a career, because they’ve got nothing to show for it,” Nelson says. “There’s no aftercare. Everybody’s running for the trees, nobody wants to take responsibility for the fighters creating the entertainment.

“The amount of household names I could tell you that are absolutely on their ass, they’ve got nothing, and that financial pressure on top of the other effects of boxing has accumulated over the years. How can your mental health be stable? How can it be?”

In general, Nelson articulates the existence of a boxer with ease.

“That animalistic instinct we have, there’s nothing you can adapt it to in everyday life – not an office or anything like that, because it’s barbaric,” he says. “It’s a very lonely existence. Your wife, brother, mother, sister don’t get it. The aches and pains are lonely, the thought processes are lonely.

“You do it first for the love of it, then money comes into it, then ups and downs, so we still do it – but resentfully. You’ve not got time to have a full-time job, so [you may think]: ‘People see me on a dizzy high, and then I’ve got to go and work on a building site. God, I've got to deal with the shame of that.’

“You’re resentful of how human nature can change: when you retire, people no longer look up to you as an amazing fighter. ‘He’s overweight, he’s not who he was.’ They talk to you like they talk to anybody, whereas when you’re a fighter, they talk to you with respect.”

Nelson is now one of the most thoughtful and respected pundits in boxing, but he could not have foreseen this future while immersed in his past.

“I thought boxing was the only option I had,” he reflects. “I left school with the reading and writing ability of a 10-year-old. I wasn’t thick – I just wasn’t academically astute – but I thought I was. I’d got nothing on paper to say, ‘Johnny is really good with people,’ so that wisdom doesn’t get you a job. What gets you a job is a diploma, work experience. So, panic set in. I could have easily ended up in prison.”

As The Final Round shows, boxing can be its own kind of prison, but a champion who escaped relatively early and safely was Anthony Crolla, who retired on a win just before turning 33.

“You can’t let boxing take more from you than you take from boxing,” he says astutely in the film. If only it were that simple.

title: PFL, Jake Paul’s MVP merge to form new global combat sports company
description: Professional Fighters League and Most Valuable Promotions have officially merged in a massive development in the world of combat sports.
fullText:
Professional Fighters League and Most Valuable Promotions have officially merged in a massive development in the world of combat sports.

 The new company will operate under the MVP banner, led by Co-Founders and Board Members Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian. Meanwhile, former PFL CEO John Martin will serve as CEO and Board Member of the new league. MVP’s boxing business and blockbuster live events will continue under Bidarian. Existing PFL shareholders 885 Capital and affiliated entities Knighthead Capital Management will be the founding investors of the new league, committing new capital.

 The new league vows to work under a “fighter-first” philosophy, seemingly challenging rival Ultimate Fighting Championship. While the UFC has been severely criticized over minimum profit share for athletes, the new combat sports league promises equitable compensation. The new league also plans to encourage athletes to build their brands inside and outside of competition, probably hinting at freedom to choose sponsors.

“We started MVP to disrupt a broken model,” Jake Paul, co-founder of Most Valuable Promotions, said in a press release. “We wanted to give fighters fair pay and a bigger, modernized stage to become global superstars. Joining forces with PFL accelerates that vision by a decade. We now have a scaled platform to give today's fans what they want: elite talent mixed with culture, lifestyle, and massive social velocity. MVP was always bigger than me and bigger than any one fighter. MVP is an inevitable movement that needs to happen for the athletes, and now we have all the resources we need to build something that changes this sport forever. I have more conviction in MVP than ever, driven by the proliferation of AI, which will only increase the value of real, live experiences and the sports properties that can bring fans closer to the athletes they love. I look forward to putting my entire promotional muscle into our new company, returning to the boxing ring and making my MVP MMA debut. To all current MVP and PFL fighters, things just got bigger. To fighters fighting in other organizations, we are open for business when you are contractually free. The time for change is now. Welcome to MVP.”

 The combined company also vows to display its capabilities by hosting five premium events across boxing and MMA in August. The brand will have 400 athletes combined under its roster and plans to invest aggressively in both sports.

 “Over the past seven years, PFL has built the world’s No. 2 global MMA company, assembling one of the sport’s most elite fighter rosters while creating a world-class global business with premier media distribution across 34 broadcast and streaming partners, reaching fans in more than 170 countries,” John Martin, chief executive officer of the new company said in a press release. “At the same time, MVP has redefined how combat sports connects with a new generation of fans, creating events that become cultural moments and proving that athletes, sports, entertainment and creators can all thrive together. This merger brings scale - in operations, in distribution and media rights, in sponsorship, in fighter development and in fan engagement. We're not just combining companies, we're bringing an entire combat sports community together and creating a more powerful platform to accelerate growth. One company, one global stage, millions of fans and we're only just getting started. I'm excited to work with Jake and Nakisa as we build the future of combat sports together, and I'm deeply grateful for the continued confidence and support of our lead investors, 885 Capital and Knighthead Capital Management.”

title: NBC Sports Philadelphia weighing adding courtside voice for Sixers after LeBron James arrival
description: NBC Sports Philadelphia is budgeting to add a courtside voice to its Sixers broadcasts ahead of LeBron James’s arrival this season, network vice president of content Alexandra Matcham told the Philadelphia Inquirer. “I think you need a voice on the court where Alaa [Abdelnaby] and Kate [Scott] can’t be to give us insight, do pre-…
fullText:
NBC Sports Philadelphia is budgeting to add a courtside voice to its Sixers broadcasts ahead of LeBron James’s arrival this season, network vice president of content Alexandra Matcham told the Philadelphia Inquirer.

“I think you need a voice on the court where Alaa [Abdelnaby] and Kate [Scott] can’t be to give us insight, do pre- and postgame interviews, analysis, all of that,” Matcham said. “It’s a very hard job to do.”

For years, NBC Sports Philadelphia and its predecessor, Comcast SportsNet, used reporters like Serena Winters and Taryn Hatcher to fill that kind of role for the Sixers. That stopped in 2020, when the network began eliminating in-arena and in-game reporting jobs across its properties as basketball and hockey seasons wrapped that year, according to Crossing Broad’s Kevin Kinkead. Hatcher stayed on covering the Phillies for five more seasons after that before her contract lapsed at the end of 2025 and NBC Sports Philadelphia cut the position rather than renew it. Kinkead later reported that the network and Hatcher had discussed a freelance arrangement that would have let her take on other work at the same time, but the talks ended without an agreement over what Kinkead’s sources described as a standard contract disagreement, not any real conflict between the two sides.

That left NBC Sports Philadelphia without anyone in that role for the Sixers’ 2025-26 season, and the roster now taking shape gives the network far less room to go another year without one.

“If you get a generational talent on your team, it could easily become a situation where the people that work for us are burnt out by December, and you don’t want that,” Matcham said. “You need extra help.”

The shape of the new role hasn’t been decided, and Matcham said she’s been deliberate about not defaulting to the title NBC Sports Philadelphia has used for that kind of position in the past. The network cut its last remaining in-arena reporting jobs across its properties, including the Sixers, starting in 2020, and whatever gets added back now won’t simply be a return to that old model.

“As I’m talking to my colleagues, I’m not even calling it a reporter role because I feel like it’s going to give them a stereotype I don’t necessarily mean,” Matcham said.

Among the options Matcham described is bypassing a generalist Sixers reporter altogether in favor of someone hired specifically for James’s orbit, someone with an existing relationship built from prior coverage of him rather than of the team broadly.

The Scott-Abdelnaby broadcast finished 29th out of 30 teams in AA’s 2025-26 local NBA announcer rankings, the third straight season in that spot. The most common grade fans gave them was a C, and roughly six in ten voters gave them a passing grade at all. Several comments also cited the absence of Hatcher as a drag on the broadcast.

Hatcher spent eight years at NBC Sports Philadelphia covering all four major Philadelphia teams, most recently working Phillies home games alongside Tom McCarthy and John Kruk, but since her departure has been selective about new roles while managing a health situation. Matcham defended the decision at the time, telling the Philadelphia Business Journal the network wanted “to add to our storytelling in new ways” and that the position was being eliminated.

Whatever title the network settles on, it will be trying to recreate, under different terms, the exact kind of presence it decided a year ago it could do without.

title: 'Time for change is now' - MVP and PFL merge
description: Most Valuable Promotions and the Professional Fighters League merge to create "a combat sports company for the new era".
fullText:
Most Valuable Promotions and the Professional Fighters League have merged to create "a combat sports company for the new era".

The newly formed partnership will be led by MVP co-founders Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian, with PFL head John Martin also on the board and continuing to operate as CEO.

The PFL will move under the brand of MVP to bring together a roster of more than 300 fighters across boxing and mixed martial arts (MMA).

MVP focused on boxing when launching in 2021 but ventured into MMA for the first time in May.

"We started MVP to disrupt a broken model," Paul said.

"We wanted to give fighters fair pay and a bigger, modernised stage to become global superstars. Joining forces with PFL accelerates that vision by a decade.

"To all current MVP and PFL fighters, things just got bigger. To fighters fighting in other organisations, we are open for business when you are contractually free. The time for change is now."

MVP's first - and only - MMA show set a new record for the most-watched MMA event in the United States, with a "minute audience" of 12.4 million viewers as Ronda Rousey beat Gina Carrano, according to broadcaster Netflix.

Rousey's 15-second win peaked at 17 million viewers globally on Netflix, shattering the previous record of nine million.

The PFL has attempted to innovate the MMA space since launching in 2017, opting for a league-based system with points gained in each fight before season-ending play-offs.

It initially offered prize money of $1m (£750,000) but made sweeping changes in 2025 and reduced that to $500,000 (£374,000).

"Over the past seven years, PFL has built the world's number two global MMA company," Martin said.

"We're not just combining companies, we're bringing an entire combat sports community together and creating a more powerful platform to accelerate growth.

"One company, one global stage, millions of fans - and we're only just getting started."

It comes after MVP announced a new partnership with Matchroom Boxing on Tuesday, with the aim of creating more opportunities for female fighters across both promotional rosters.

MVP has invested heavily in women's boxing over the past five years and boasts an impressive stable of world champions, including Britons Caroline Dubois and Chantelle Cameron.

title: Cricket & archery well placed for Commonwealths spot
description: Cricket, archery and shooting are among the sports well placed to regain their spot at the Commonwealth Games in India in 2030.
fullText:
Cricket, archery and shooting are among the sports well placed to regain their spot at the Commonwealth Games in India in 2030.

Only 10 sports were included in the ongoing Glasgow Games because of the rushed build-up after the Australian state of Victoria pulled out as hosts.

Discussions on the sporting programme remain ongoing between Commonwealth Sport, sporting federations and the Indian organising committee for the next Games, which will be held in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.

Speaking to BBC Sport, Commonwealth Sport chief executive Katie Sadlier would not be drawn on the process but India Olympic Association's Raghu Iyer said: "There are many sports who will feel they have missed out.

"There are sports in which India has done very well, shooting, archery and many other sports."

Pushed on whether that puts cricket, which was included for Birmingham 2022 for the first time in 24 years as a women's-only T20 event, archery and shooting at the top of the queue, Iyer added: "While I do not have the mandate to talk about any of these, you have been pretty interesting with the choices you have mentioned…"

"We also want to have sports that India have traditionally done well in," he said.

Boxer Abdul - grandson of dictator - disqualified for headbutt

Cricket's cause is helped by the fact at least two team sports will be added for 2030. Hockey and rugby sevens would be other options.

Badminton, 3x3 basketball and 3x3 wheelchair basketball, beach volleyball, cycling, diving, judo, rhythmic gymnastics, squash, triathlon and para triathlon and wrestling are other sports under consideration.

India can also propose two new sports as host nation and push others that have significance at home. No final decisions have been made.

Ahmedabad will be the Commonwealth's centenary Games and events will held in the 120,000-seater Narendra Modi Stadium, which has hosted two cricket World Cup finals in recent years.

India has also expressed a keen interest in hosting the 2036 Olympic Games, with this potentially a key step in the road.

"Any sporting event will be a step towards that," Iyer said. "We are looking purely at ensuring that these Commonwealth Games are one of the best that have been held."

The reduced programme in Glasgow has helped slash the cost of hosting the Games from around £800m to £160m.

Organisers have been keen to claim this repurposed structure will be cheaper and more appealing for future hosts, but the sporting programme will rise to 17 in Ahmedabad.

"17 is, we think, the right number," Sadlier said.

"The Victoria Games was 26 sports. We recognised we needed to reset and bring the Games into something that was affordable around the Commonwealth.

"What we have done here has been brilliant but we will bring back a few sports. We won't go beyond that number."

Sadlier also rejected concerns around the cut through of the Glasgow Games, given there has been no live television coverage on a major channel in the UK.

"We have got more broadcast deals signed for this Games than we ever have," she said.

"Globally, the reach has been exceptional. On socials we broke the targets from Birmingham last week. It has been an amazingly covered Games."

fullText:

title: Brazil bans defender Gabriel until Pec returns from broken leg injury
description: Internacional's Victor Gabriel is suspended until Cruzeiro forward Gabriel Pec returns from a broken left leg, Brazil's sports court said.
fullText:
July 29 (UPI) -- Internacional's Victor Gabriel is suspended until Cruzeiro forward Gabriel Pec returns from a broken left leg injury, Brazil's sports court said.

Brazil's Superior Court of Sports Justice, or STJD, announced the ruling Tuesday. Pec fractured a tibia after Gabriel tackled him during a 2-1 win over Internacional on July 22 in Porto Alegre, Brazil.

Gabriel, who attended the STJD committee hearing for the ruling, apologized to Pec.

"I had the feeling that I would get to the ball first, and I did," Gabriel said. "Since the field was quite slippery and wet, I ended up hitting the ball and then I didn't have time to pull my leg back, and that's how this somewhat harder tackle happened, but without any intention of causing harm to my fellow professional or any malice."

The defender was given a red card for the incident. Pec's injury required surgery. Gabriel's ban, which will end when Pec returns to training, is capped at 180 days.

"I've always been a loyal guy and I've always gone onto the field to, above all, defend my club and my dream," Gabriel said. "I've always tried to be as loyal as possible to my teammates and opponents. It was a completely unfortunate incident.

"I apologized to him and offered my help. I asked him to forgive me for not having had any ill intent, and all I could do at that moment was pray for him.

"Since that night, it's been incredibly difficult for me. My whole life I've prepared for moments of happiness, and instead, it's been sleepless nights."

Internacional (5-9-6) sits at No. 16 in the Brazilian Serie A standings. Cruzeiro (7-7-6) sits at No. 11, 17 points behind first-place Palmeiras (13-2-5).

title: LeBron James, 76ers To Be Showcased 34 Times On National TV

fullText:
LeBron James and the new-look Philadelphia 76ers will be showcased 34 times on national television during the 2026-27 NBA season, according to Front Office Sports.

That is the maximum number allocated across Disney’s ABC/ESPN, NBCUniversal’s NBC Sports/Peacock, and Amazon’s Prime Video.

NBA Commissioner Adam Silver said before the 41-year-old James dropped his latest decision last Friday that the league was waiting for James to release its schedule.

Among the highly anticipated matchups for the 76ers, who will feature a starting five of James, Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid will be their games against the reigning NBA champion New York Knicks; Brown’s former team, the Boston Celtics; the new-look Miami Heat featuring Giannis Antetokounmpo; James’ first team, the Cleveland Cavaliers; James’ most recent team, the L.A. Lakers; and Steph Curry and the Golden State Warriors, a team James considered before choosing the Sixers.

"I would like him to make his announcement already, so we can finish the schedule, because, as you might imagine, the teams are calling us, the networks are calling us, and everybody wants to lock in the schedule," Silver said before James’ decision.

“But it will influence how we set the schedule, how we set opening week, Christmas Day, etc. So I need him to make a decision.”

In the wake of James’ latest move, the 76ers jumped to the third favorite behind the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder to win the NBA title, ahead of the Knicks and 2024 NBA champion Celtics.

title: Falcons land WR help in 2027 NFL mock draft from CBS Sports
description: Falcons take 6-foot-3 Texas WR in 2027 NFL mock draft from CBS Sports
fullText:
There are some major question marks surrounding the Atlanta Falcons' roster as the team prepares to kick off training camp this week in Flowery Branch. From the starting quarterback competition to the battle for the No. 2 wide receiver job, Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski has much to figure out over the next month.

The team signed former first-round pick Jahan Dotson to replace speedster Darnell Mooney, but it's fair to question whether or not he's capable of filling that role. Dotson's career stats suggest otherwise, however, it's tough to produce when you're stuck behind two elite receivers, as he was in Philadelphia.

Former Georgia wide receiver Zachariah Branch appears to have a bright future, assuming his effectiveness isn't hindered by his lack of size. Depending on how this season goes, the Falcons may or may not be looking for a new No. 2 wide receiver in 2027.

Atlanta lands a perfect complement to Drake London in a new CBS Sports mock draft from Mike Renner. The Falcons were projected to take Texas wide receiver Cam Coleman with the sixth overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.

"Cam Coleman is a wildly explosive 6-foot-3, 200-pound wideout who spent the past two seasons stuck with poor quarterback play at Auburn," wrote Renner. "That changes this year as he heads to Texas to pair with Arch Manning. He should be a household name by season's end."

Coleman racked up 93 receptions for 1,306 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns (14.0 yards per catch) over the last two seasons at Auburn. The Falcons have dealt with similar quarterback issues over the past few years, so Coleman would feel right at home in Atlanta.

The Falcons did re-sign London to a four-year, $141 million contract extension during the offseason, however, there is still a clear lack of depth behind him. Branch could be a long-term option in the slot with No. 2 upside, but it wouldn't hurt to add to the receiver room in 2027.

For now, Atlanta is set to kick off training camp with its current wide receiver group. Although, we wouldn't be surprised to see the team add someone like Stefon Diggs or Keenan Allen before camp ends.

title: Italy’s Sports minister slams Azzurri’s Andrea Pirlo mess-up
description: Italian football finds itself in the middle of a crisis again, as Andrea Pirlo’s candidacy for the Azzurri role has gone up in smoke. There have been increasing doubts about the future of Paolo Mald...
fullText:
Italian football finds itself in the middle of a crisis again, as Andrea Pirlo’s candidacy for the Azzurri role has gone up in smoke. There have been increasing doubts about the future of Paolo Maldini too and now, Italy’s sports minister Andrea Abodi has made his views clear about the matter.

Now, Pirlo will definitely not be the next manager of the national team. This is largely due to his links with a FonBet, a Russian betting company and this didn’t sit well with many at FIGC, even if it went against the technical director Maldini’s wishes.

Now, Abodi has been asked about the matter and he has made it clear that things like these shouldn’t be happening in Calcio.

He told Piacenza Hub Network – via Di Marzio: Pirlo’s resignation from the Azzurri bench? It’s news that speaks for itself. It’s a situation we would have liked to have changed with greater speed and with a shared purpose that hasn’t materialised. Now we have to make up for a poor showing.”

The outcome of the Pirlo saga is arguably something that can only unfold in Italian football, embarrassingly enough. It is a classic case of putting politics over sport, while hiring a sporting figure who should be backed to the helm. This is what lets Italian football down – from top to bottom, and it has happened again.

title: USA250: The 10 greatest college athletes from Nebraska
description: As part of USA TODAY Sports' USA 250 initiative, here's a look at the top 10 greatest college athletes to ever play in the state of Nebraska:
fullText:
Nebraska is a fascinating state to delve into in regard to college sports history, as it has a burgeoning sports scene without the imposing influence of professional sports.

The University of Nebraska's Memorial Stadium has sold out since the 1960s. The College World Series takes place in Omaha. Nebraska women's volleyball holds the world record for attendance at a women's sporting event.

And it isn't just a matter of circumstance. The programs built the loyalty. The Tom Osborne Nebraska-Oklahoma-Barry Switzer football rivalry is the stuff of legend, the 1990s Cornhuskers are still spoken of in reverential tones. Creighton basketball went from Missouri Valley powerhouse to Big East staple. And Nebraska women's volleyball has one of the most passionate followings among college sports as a whole.

From all of that loyalty is borne legendary figures. Across the state and across sports, Nebraska has the athletes to run with nearly any state in the country. Paring that list down to 10 proved to be an extremely difficult task. But here are the 10 Nebraska college athletes who managed to set themselves apart.

Nebraska of the 1990s was dominant. And Tommie Frazier was one of the team's great players in the decade. After he got his feet wet as a freshman, Frazier came into his own as a sophomore. Though he rarely threw the ball in Tom Osborne's ruthless triple option offense, but he passed for 3,521 yards in his career and added 1,955 yards and 36 touchdowns on the ground. But Frazier's legacy defies stats: Nebraska won 36 of 37 games in his final three seasons. The lone loss came to Florida State at the end of the 1993 season in the Orange Bowl that was a matchup of two unbeatens. Frazier would then lead the Cornhuskers to back-to-back titles the next two season and finish runner-up to Eddie George in the voting for the 1995 Heisman Trophy.

USA 250 LISTS: Alaska | Alabama | Arizona | Arkansas | California | Colorado | Connecticut | Delaware | Florida | Georgia | Hawaii | Idaho | Illinois | Indiana | Iowa | Kansas | Kentucky | Louisiana | Maine | Maryland | Massachusetts | Michigan | Minnesota | Mississippi | Missouri | Montana | Nebraska | Nevada | New Hampshire | New Jersey

Born in Omaha in 1935, Bob Gibson is one of the most dynamic pitchers in baseball history. His stuff is the stuff of legends, and he got his start with the Creighton Bluejays. A two-sport athlete, Gibson played baseball and basketball for his hometown university. He finished his career on the hardwood as the school's third-leading scorer at the time with 1,272 points. Unfortunately, his baseball stats are lost in the annals of history, it's known he was an outfielder and a pitcher for Creighton. Gibson had a legendary pitching career with the St. Louis Cardinals, and was named to Creighton's Hall of Fame in 1968.

When you think about hard-nosed Huskers, you think about Mike Rozier. After setting the single-season school record with 1,689 rushing yards as a junior in 1982, he shattered his own mark the following season as part of one of the greatest offenses in college history. Rozier put up an absurd 2,148 yards and an NCAA-record 29 touchdowns on the ground on his way to winning the 1983 Heisman Trophy. That Nebraska offense averaged over 50 points per game with Rozier serving as the focal point, and though it came up short of a national title with an Orange Bowl loss to Miami, it's remembered as one of the great seasons in Nebraska football.

PROGRAM RANKINGS: Top 25 | Big Ten | SEC | ACC | Big 12

Ask someone born in the '90s the most dominant defensive player they watched in college growing up, and dollars to donuts Ndamukong Suh's name is going to come up. One of the most overpowering linemen in history, Suh turned otherwise-stalwart offensive linemen into sleds. Suh's 2009 season is the stuff of college football legend: He finished fourth in Heisman Trophy voting, the best at the time for a solely defensive player since Steve Emtman in 1991 after logging 85 tackles with 20½ tackles for a loss and 12 sacks. Suh missing out on the Heisman was widely regarded as a death knell for the hopes of a solely defensive player winning the trophy, and he remains a Nebraska legend to this day.

Johnny Rodgers isn't just etched into the fabric of Nebraska. He's woven into the tapestry of college football. A receiver, running back, and return specialist, record after record fell before Rodgers' speed. A Walter Camp Player of the Year and Heisman Trophy winner in 1971, Rodgers finished his career with the two highest all-purpose yards seasons in Nebraska history, along with the record for most career all-purpose yards. He still holds the record for career receiving touchdowns and ended his time on the gridiron with the most points accounted for in Nebraska history. Often considered among the best return men in college football history, Rodgers was precursor for the athlete position in college sports.

Eric Crouch evokes one of the last gasps of an era of greatness for Nebraska football. Crouch led the Big 12 in rushing touchdowns in each of his final three seasons and posted a 35-7 record as a starter. He had a dominant senior campaign in 2001 to win the Heisman Trophy, edging out Florida quarterback Rex Grossman. For the season, Crouch rushed for 1,115 yards and 18 touchdowns and threw for 1,510 yards, while leading the Cornhuskers to the Bowl Championship Series title game in the Rose Bowl. Though Nebraska would lose to Miami (Fla.) in his final game, Crouch's legacy has endured as one of the most dynamic athletes in Cornhusker football history.

While Nebraska football is a dynasty, Nebraska volleyball is an institution all of its own. The Cornhuskers are five-time national champions and have four championships since the turn of the century. Pavan is one of the most decorated volleyball players in Nebraska history. She was a four-time first-team All-American and set multiple records with the Cornhuskers while making Lincoln a destination for volleyball. Pavan helped Nebraska to a national championship in 2006 and four consecutive Big 12 titles. She is quintessentially Nebraska volleyball, and volleyball is quintessentially Nebraska.

Why wouldn't Nebraska get two volleyball players on this list? Joining Pavan is Jordan Larson, who was also part of the 2006 championship team. Larson was a three-time All-American and had over 1,000 kills and digs in her Nebraska career. Her best season was in 2008, when she earned multiple accolades before becoming an Olympic star as well, culminating in a gold medal win in Tokyo in the 2020 Summer Games.

Fresh off her college career when she was a four-time first-team All-American, Frahm is already a Nebraska softball legend. Born in Papillion, Frahm started her career at Oklahoma, winning two national championships with a 44-2 record as the star pitcher for Sooners. Frahm transferred to Nebraska after her sophomore season, but was injured in her first game in 2024. She returned the following year to help Nebraska to the super regionals for the first time since 2014. Frahm was national player of the year as a senior, leading the Cornhuskers to their first Women's College World Series appearance since 2013,. A true two-way superstar, she posted a 47-14 record pitching over two seasons at Nebraska with an ERA of 1.44. She slugged 1.418 as a Cornhusker with 43 home runs.

title: Holders St Mirren draw Rangers in League Cup last 16
description: Holders St Mirren are drawn away to Rangers in the last 16 of the Premier Sports Cup, while Celtic visit Dundee United.
fullText:
Holders St Mirren have been drawn away to Rangers in the last 16 of the Premier Sports Cup.

There are two other all top-flight ties, with Scottish champions Celtic, who were last season's beaten finalists, visiting Dundee United while Aberdeen host Dundee.

Top-flight Kilmarnock will host Ayr United in an Ayrshire derby.

At least one side outwith the Premiership is guaranteed to reach the quarter-finals after second-tier Dunfermline Athletic were drawn at home to League 1 side Ross County.

Dunfermline beat holders St Mirren as both progress in League Cup

St Johnstone crash out as Dundee Utd squeeze through - League Cup round-up

Dunfermline were the last side to qualify for the last 16 when a late Chris Kane penalty secured a win away to St Mirren on Sunday that sealed progress as one of the three best runners-up at Championship rivals Queen's Park's expense.

Although St Mirren still topped the group on goal difference, the defeat meant they missed out on being seeded in Sunday's draw.

Reacting to being drawn away to Rangers, manager Craig McLeish said: "I am disappointed from my point of view that we had a chance to win our group and be one of the seeded sides and the draw has not been good to us.

"I thought we were denied a goal, but we only have ourselves to blame unfortunately."

Dunfermline head coach Neil Lennon was a happier man.

"I thought we played well in the last half hour and deserved our victory," he said.

"A home tie is the most important thing, but Ross County have been phenomenal this season after a hugely disappointing relegation, so we will not be taking anything for granted."

Aberdeen, Ayr, Dundee United, Inverness Caledonian Thistle, Kilmarnock, County and Stenhousemuir were the other group winners, while Dundee and Partick Thistle progressed as runners-up.

Celtic, Heart of Midlothian, Hibernian, Motherwell and Rangers were given byes to the last 16 as they are representing Scotland in European competitions.

While the Old Firm have been drawn against top-flight opponents, the other three take on Championship sides, with Hearts hosting Caley Thistle, Hibs at home to Partick Thistle and Motherwell away to Stenhousemuir.

The second-round ties will be played on the weekend of 15-16 August.
